notes: Procedural depth plus the stabilization table in NFM A6.8. Claims: mp-60s-surface-water-06 and mp-60s-groundwater-03 (minimum 60 seconds at each new measurement location for the sensors and sonde body to reach thermal equilibrium), mp-60s-longer-manufacturer-07 (the 60 seconds is a minimum only), mp-equilibrium-range-04 (60 seconds to several minutes depending on instrument and temperature difference), mp-stabilize-to-table-01 and mp-t5-temperature-03 / -sc-04 / -do-05 / -ph-06 / -turbidity-07 (table 6.8-5 criteria). Turn 2 is the follow-up an operator asks once told to wait: how do I know it is done. Expected to favor rag: the slice's probe datasheets give sensor response times (1 second to 90 or 95 percent of reading), which is a plausible-looking wrong answer to turn 1, and give no stabilization criteria at all for turn 2.

turns.content: When we shift the sonde to a new spot in the creek, how long do we have to leave it there before the readings are worth writing down?

must_contain: States a minimum of 60 seconds at each new measurement location
Explains the wait is for the sensors and the sonde body to reach the water's temperature
States the 60 seconds is a floor and some instruments need longer per the manufacturer
Notes equilibration can run from 60 seconds to several minutes depending on the temperature difference
must_not: Invents a shorter wait such as 30 seconds
Presents 60 seconds as always sufficient rather than a minimum
Uses a probe datasheet's 1-second response time as the settling time

turns.content: Once we've waited, how do I know the numbers have actually settled and aren't still creeping?

must_contain: States temperature must be stable within ±0.2 °C
States dissolved oxygen must be stable within ±0.2 mg/L
States pH must be stable within ±0.1 unit
States specific conductance must be within ±5 µS/cm at or below 100 µS/cm, and ±3 percent above 100 µS/cm
States turbidity must be within ±0.5 turbidity units or 5 percent, whichever is greater
must_not: Invents a stabilization tolerance not in the table
Gives the operator baseline healthy ranges instead of stabilization criteria
Gives criteria for only one or two of the parameters when asked about the sonde as a whole
